What the trend says

SLV: growth followed by a sharp slowdown

Gross metal flows rose from 507.0m oz in 2024 to 680.7m oz in 2025 (+34.3%). Q1 2026 then reached 223.6m oz; Q2 fell to 68.5m oz (-69.4% quarter on quarter).

Direction matters as much as total activity

SLV H1 2026 gross activity was only 1.5% below H1 2025, but redemptions exceeded creations by 47.7m oz. IAU also saw net withdrawals; IAUM saw net additions. A single assumption about flow direction would miss these differences.

The Irish series have different growth patterns

Annual gross flows increased 35.4% for silver, 68.0% for platinum and 27.1% for palladium. Unhedged gold declined 12.7%; the two hedged gold series grew from much smaller bases.

Canada: gold and silver diverge

Combining both classes, H1 2026 gross gold activity was 21.0m units, down 20.0% from H1 2025. Silver was 4.75m units, up 72.7%. These are fund units, not bar ounces.

Swiss gold: distinct mandates

In the year to May 2026, CSGOLD issued 1.00m and redeemed 0.26m units. CHF-hedged gold issued 0.42m and redeemed 0.392m. EUR-hedged gold issued 0.308m and redeemed 0.616m.

Evidence already in their documentation

38 specific findings, each mapped to the funds it covers and linked to the relevant agreement, clause or report page. These turn the research agenda into documented points for the discussion.

SLV

Exit / migration

“180 Business Days”

Documented: Ordinary termination requires at least 180 business days’ written notice. Storage fees continue pending acceptable redelivery arrangements.

For the pitch: Start exit planning and fee negotiation early.

Still to obtain: Current fee schedule; agreed accelerated exit; bar-release throughput.

Custodian agreement §12.1–12.2

IAU

Exit / migration

Documented: Ordinary termination requires at least 180 business days’ notice; redelivery and continuing fees need to be addressed.

For the pitch: IAU also needs a negotiated migration timetable.

Still to obtain: Current amendments and transition terms.

Custodian agreement §12.1–12.2

IAUM

Exit / migration

Documented: Ordinary termination requires at least 180 business days’ notice, with redelivery arrangements and continuing charges.

For the pitch: Do not assume a quicker switch for the smaller trust.

Still to obtain: Current amendments and transition terms.

Custodian agreement §13.1–13.2

SLV

Order data / reconciliation

“identifying separately each transaction”

Documented: Next-business-day reporting by 9am New York identifies individual movements and substitutions; records contain bar and transaction detail.

For the pitch: The contractual reporting chain supports requesting actual gross daily activity.

Still to obtain: 36 months of timestamped orders, bars, vaults, failures and cancellations.

Custodian agreement(s) §2.5(a)–(c), §2.8

IAU; IAUM

Order data / reconciliation

Documented: Both gold contracts require individual movement reporting and account records; a daily net share series is an inferior substitute.

For the pitch: Request custodian records from the trustee rather than estimating gross activity from share changes.

Still to obtain: Matching order and bar-level extracts for both trusts.

Custodian agreement(s) §2.5(a)–(c), §2.8 · Supporting document

SLV

Substitution / composition

“With your prior approval”

Documented: Substitutions need prior trustee approval in consultation with the sponsor, preserving ounces and fine weight.

For the pitch: Potential route to improving US-origin composition in London and New York.

Still to obtain: Standing approval process, pricing, tax and eligible replacements.

Custodian agreement §2.7, §9.2(e)

IAU; IAUM

Earlier pitch calculations rechecked

The September deployment example retains its original 70,168,993.4 oz New York balance and $65/oz scenario price. Its fixed 50% pool is 35,084,496.7 oz. These historical assumptions have not been silently replaced with October holdings.

CaseOunces deployedCapture / ozGross captureHalf each before costs
Initial deferred position3,508,449.67$0.500$1,754,224.84$877,112.42

20% tariff alternative14,033,798.68$11.050$155,073,475.41$77,536,737.71

The 10% and 20% tariff cases are alternatives; their proceeds are not added. The initial deferred result is separate. The contractual payment concept is 50% each of realised net trading revenue, so half of gross capture is not the final payable amount.

The 250,000-oz / 50-lot example at $60/oz gives $125,000 spread capture, $20,000 shipment assumption, $1.5m cash initial margin and $1,250 monthly funding cost at 1% annually. After one month and those two costs: $103,750, or $51,875 each. It is not a guaranteed trade result; other costs and the exit/delivery economics must be modelled.

Silver composition charts

The 9 October chart arithmetic reconciles: London 493,474 bars (SLV plus the Irish silver ETC), USA 66,897 bars (SLV only). US-produced bars are 1,325 / 493,474 = 0.27% in London and 26,544 / 66,897 = 39.68% in New York. At a fixed NY total, reaching at least 50% requires 6,905 additional US-produced bars replacing other bars.

The country aggregation and percentages were rechecked. Individual historic refinery assignments were not all independently re-researched in this audit. “USSR” remains a legacy stamp classification, not a verified present-day country. Refinery country does not by itself establish customs origin or tariff exemption.

Points that cannot be presented as established facts

  • JPMorgan’s negotiated SLV storage and handling rates: the fee letters/invoices remain private. Published COMEX maximum tariffs are comparators, not SLV prices.
  • Custody versus trading title: trustee-authorised release or bar selection does not automatically transfer the client’s metal to Citi’s trading desk. The ownership and payment arrangements need their own documented route. Current ETF bars have not been shown to be on CME warrant.
  • Capacity and execution readiness: discussions with major providers and available space are desk-supplied commercial evidence. Signed capacity, throughput, insurance and transition terms remain needed; the public filings do not prove them.
  • Tariff and capture scenarios: 10%/20% tariffs, 85% capture, deployable fractions, $0.08/oz shipment and 10% cash initial margin are assumptions. Neither the filing audit nor the calculations validate tariff probabilities or expected profit.
  • Dividend claim: a broad “first precious-metals ETF dividend” is unsupported. GLDN reports an AUD242,000 distribution in its 2026 annual report. A narrower location-revenue-funded dividend is a proposal; its first-ever status and legal/tax mechanism are unproven. GLDN Note 4, PDF p25.
  • New locations and products: Irish platinum/palladium US storage, India/China bonded access and broader bar formats require the appropriate mandate and customs analysis. Bonded status alone does not establish regulatory permission.

Source integrity and audit boundary

The index contains 1,542 records: 1,278 stored-file hash checks matched, with zero mismatches. The other 264 records are logged failed retrievals (24) or unavailable dated holdings (240), not verified evidence. Record counts include repeated source entries and are not counts of unique documents.

All 82 URLs in the pre-correction core holdings, flow and evidence dataset resolved: 51 by direct HTTP checks and 31 SEC documents through the web retrieval tool after direct requests returned 403. The newly added IAU 2020 amendment link was independently opened as well. URL accessibility and byte integrity alone do not prove that every claim in every archived document is correct.

This review covers the latest full-fund research pack, its underlying financial-document extracts, the material custody provisions, and the earlier deployment/origin arithmetic described above. Earlier news, EFP observations, every historical refiner mapping and every private commercial claim have not all been freshly re-underwritten. The report does not assert that every archived presentation, exported Word/PDF version or live webpage has been revised. The current research report and workbook are the corrected outputs.

What else would help win the custody mandate?

The strongest commercial case would combine an evidenced net-revenue opportunity, a competitive all-in custody price, and a transition that maintains dealing service. The following research would turn the proposition into terms BlackRock can evaluate.

Where could gross daily creation and redemption records come from?

Authorised participants: each participant may be able to supply its own executed orders and settlement records.
